rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 9's '**The point:**' now prints Klaassen's current 8-stage form in full — 'ideate → brainstorm → plan → work → review → polish → compound → repeat' — replacing the retired 4-step form. Three independent strategy-doc conflicts, not just a length judgment: (1) content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md § 'Woven design rules' #1 (line 136) states the canonical form for THIS purpose is 'Plan → Work → Review → Compound (Klaassen)... M1's Debrief is canonical and teaches the full move once, in full' — the 4-step form, not the 8-step one; line 159 is more explicit still: 'Klaassen's four-step loop at M1 resolves "I don't know where compounding starts."' The pedagogical bet at M1 is named simplicity, not currency — the exercise body now diverges from the strategy doc's own stated design rationale for this exact beat, and per curriculum/CLAUDE.md's Alignment rule ('Strategy and module file change in the same edit. Drift = process bug') that divergence is unresolved, not a considered joint update — confirmed against the prior story-judge run on this file (this same instance file, 2026-08-01), which PASSED §4 by matching the OLD 4-step form against the strategy doc as it then read; today's body edit broke that match without a corresponding strategy-doc edit. (2) content-strategy line 278: 'Klaassen attribution happens inside Claude's Ex3 retro summary — the retro prompt asks Claude to name the shape and cite the practitioner if one fits. Peer recognition, not a lecture.' The compound-and-close-1 prompt (expanded body) still asks Claude to do exactly this — 'name 2–3 practitioners whose published work runs a similar loop... Worth surfacing if they fit: Cherny, Klaassen, Ronacher, Pocock, Karpathy, Willison' — but the body now names Klaassen and the full loop itself, one paragraph above the fence, before the student has run the prompt. The prompt's own designed discovery/recognition payoff is pre-empted by the body that precedes it. (3) The 8-stage chain names 'plan' as a loop stage inside the same module whose strategy doc calls out 'No plan mode in M1. Restraint is deliberate — M2 owns plan-mode-at-depth on multi-file work... M1 teaches where plan mode doesn't earn its keep, by contrast.' Printing 'plan' in M1's own opening frame blunts that contrast before M2 gets to make it. Separately from the strategy conflicts: locatability regressed. The retired 4-step form ended on 'Compound' — terminal position, maximal salience. The new form buries it 7th-of-8, unbolded, indistinguishable in weight from 6 words ('ideate,' 'brainstorm,' 'polish' among them) that are not yet curriculum vocabulary anywhere before this line (verified: no hits in orient-and-introspect.md, fix-tests-first.md, or getting-going.md). The sentence's own grammatical subject ('the compound step') already tells the reader what to look for; the arrow-chain then makes them hunt for it instead of see it. The backing block (lines 74, 84-85) shows this was a deliberate, cost-aware maintainer call, not an oversight — logged per §51's accepted-by-design pattern is the right home if kept, but on the merits this doesn't yet earn the cost: it buries the very word it's meant to spotlight, and it fights the strategy doc's own stated reason for using the simple form at M1 specifically.
